key_insight: An integrated deep learning and adaptive-control method aims to help GMAW robots adjust welding parameters as joint conditions change.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets reduced manual reprogramming and more consistent weld quality despite machining errors, assembly deviations and thermal changes.
method: Combine quality-grade-oriented planning with site-specific multi-objective parameter optimization.
Use semi-supervised semantic segmentation to perceive weld seams and molten pools, alongside neural-network weld-formation prediction for spatter suppression.
Apply fuzzy adaptive control to adjust the welding process.
evidence_signal: Experiments used Q235 carbon-steel butt joints and developed a response-surface model linking welding current, speed, torch angle and nozzle height to weld geometry.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative performance gains, and applicability beyond Q235 butt joints remains unestablished.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Welding Process Optimization and Adaptive Control Method for Welding Robots
